session_read: Three stops fired and three new names landed, and the net of it is a materially healthier book: drawdown -3.25% against -10.62% three sessions ago, cash back to 8.49% from effectively zero. The stops did something the desk had been asking for and something it had been arguing against, in the same week -- COHR's trim was fulfilled exactly as proposed, while GOOGL's stop took out a position the desk had recommended topping up four separate times. That underweight (Compute/Hyperscaler 9.59% vs a 15% floor) is now the largest drift on the book, and the honest response is a $400 token conditional on GOOGL holding above $365, not a $1,200 buy into a name still falling with its founders' AI bench walking out the door. The single-factor number got worse on inspection, not better: reclassifying LRCX lifts true AI-capex to 95.0% of equity. MP and NOW are real diversification intent, but 2.7% of the book is a gesture, not a hedge. QBTS and CEG report tomorrow. Hold the cash through it.
